dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the sentencing memorandum and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The courthouse hot desks review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I completed a sentencing memorandum in the library consultation room after reading the mitigation records in sequence.
What did that protect?
It kept the family history connected to the requested sentence.
Someone new shadowed me in the Thursday morning hearing this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the library consultation room into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
I tried to draft a mitigation memorandum at a courthouse hot desk while lawyers and clients asked for help.
What happened?
I lost the treatment chronology and filed an incomplete first version.
I can return client calls from the courthouse hot desks between appearances.
Do those calls go well?
Yes, when each call has one immediate purpose.
I archived last cycle's notes on the courthouse hot desks and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The library consultation room is available from 07:00 to 09:30, but the hot-desk rotation begins at 09:00.
Could both be managed?
Only if the last half hour of the rotation is covered by another supervisor.
A vendor call about the sentencing memorandum ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the Thursday morning hearing checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the library consultation room.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the courthouse hot desks records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
At a courthouse hot desk before an earlier sentencing hearing, urgent questions from two attorneys made me skip a treatment letter and the memorandum lacked its key timeline.
Did the judge receive the complete context?
No, I had to supplement the record afterward.
I sketched next week's plan for the library consultation room before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the sentencing memorandum updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The client meeting ends at 09:30, leaving no later gap before the hearing calendar opens.
Can you finish the memorandum after the rotation starts?
No, the final review must be done before I meet the client.
The chief judge says being visible at the hot desks would reassure the calendar staff.
Does that settle the memorandum issue?
No, the hearing needs the complete mitigation record.
I closed the week by updating the Thursday morning hearing handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Why would I agree to the courthouse hot-desk rotation only with coverage during my sentencing-memorandum block?
